title: arXiv AI papers — Friday, 6 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from independently surfaced technical discussion, cross-list breadth and reported evaluation evidence. Semantic Scholar citation evidence is limited for such recent work; all selected papers had zero citations and zero influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
sections.abstract: SwarmEvolve coordinates hundreds of latent-space LLM agents through KV-cache sharing and reports faster, higher-scoring program search than three text-based frameworks on 21 mathematical and scientific-computing problems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a latent-agent evolutionary-search framework using hidden-state novelty filtering and KV-cache crossover; on their benchmark, it reaches baseline 60-minute scores in a median 3–8 minutes.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to 21 selected tasks and Qwen3 8B/14B/32B-FP8 comparisons under the paper's one-GPU, 60-minute setup; performance on other models and search workloads is not established here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Several technical writeups surfaced independently, including OpenTrain and AGI Hunt; the paper spans AI and neural/evolutionary computing and reports a multi-baseline, 21-problem evaluation. These are discussion signals, not readership counts.

sections.title: TCSExam: Evaluating Frontier LLMs on the Full Range of TCS Research
sections.abstract: TCSExam evaluates agents on theorem proving, solver engineering, constructions and open-conjecture tasks, with Lean or executable checking, and reports independently verified special cases and bounds from some attempts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute a 100-task Full suite and a 20-task Lite suite covering four kinds of TCS output; in the reported runs, Full and Lite rankings agreed strongly across eight shared agents (Spearman ρ=0.93).
sections.unique_caveat: The capability claims are bounded by the authors' curated 100-task suite, its task-specific scoring and selected evaluated agents; the suite cannot by itself establish performance across all theoretical-computer-science research.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The benchmark drew substantive external discussion from Crashtech and AIModeling; its two-category listing and four distinct, checkable task tracks add technical relevance beyond a leaderboard mention.

sections.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
sections.abstract: StepBack preserves a draft's earlier reasoning and resamples from an estimated first-error step; the authors report average accuracy matching self-consistency across seven math and multi-hop QA benchmarks with up to 41.26% fewer generated tokens.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose rollback-point selection using step-level negative log-likelihood or process-reward-model signals, followed by suffix resampling and standard majority voting.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say their experiments mainly cover mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA and use two localization signals; generalization to code generation and long-context summarization remains untested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Recent technical discussion appeared in Ken Ashe's analysis and GlobalTechDigest; the paper also has three core-category listings and a NeurIPS 2026 comment on arXiv.

sections.title: Agent-R²: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
sections.abstract: Agent-R² synthesizes productivity-agent training tasks from real occupational seeds, workflow evidence and web-sourced files, then reports results for a 4B model trained on 4,000 rubric-scored instances.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that Agent-R²-4B, trained with supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, scored 51.0% on GDPval and 14.8% on OfficeQA, above the named Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 baseline on those reported metrics.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is for one 4B model and two benchmark suites, using 4,000 synthesized training instances; results do not establish transfer to other workflows, file collections or evaluation rubrics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper received rapid indexed coverage on ModelScope and ArXivSignals; the concrete comparison spans GDPval and OfficeQA and the reported data pipeline targets realistic multi-file work.

sections.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
sections.abstract: Scientist World turns research papers into executable environments and reports 1,000 verified environments, 6,400 research-trace hours, and gains for agents evaluated against reproduced author methods.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a pipeline that extracts a paper's question, reproduces its method as a baseline and records agent experiments; they report frontier agents exceeding the reproduced human baseline in 74% of evaluations.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison depends on the fidelity of automated environment construction and reproduction of each paper's method; outperforming that baseline is not equivalent to independently validating the scientific significance of an agent's result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Multiple technical writeups appeared quickly, including Franklin He and AIModels.fyi; its three-category cross-list and training/evaluation corpus make it one of the batch's broadest research-agent contributions.

sections.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
sections.abstract: The authors propose continuous benchmark validation and report that their Terminal-Bench 2.0 audit found issues in roughly 30% of tasks, with repairs changing accuracy and some leaderboard positions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine community reports, task artifacts, agent traces, oracle checks and human-gated repairs, and argue that time/resource budgets should be maintained as part of benchmark specifications.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported 30% issue rate and score changes concern Terminal-Bench 2.0 and this audit workflow; they should not be generalized to all agent benchmarks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Discussed by Agentic Design and linked to the Terminal-Bench 2.1 release note; it also has a public OpenReview record, so its ideas were visible beyond the new arXiv listing.

sections.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
sections.abstract: Multimodal-SEA presents 608 simulated social-engineering tasks and reports that multimodal content raised attack success against seven evaluated models from 19.9% to 29.2%, with some safety settings also causing excessive refusal.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce an interactive benchmark with 608 tasks across 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios, using simulated applications and tool-execution logs to assess agent security.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluations use simulated applications and a designed set of fraud scenarios; real-world attack prevalence and transfer to deployed agents are not measured by this benchmark alone.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Rapid coverage appeared on OpenTrain and ModelScope; the task count, bilingual scenario framing and measurable security/usability trade-off make it a concrete safety-evaluation contribution.

sections.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
sections.abstract: RoboARCade evaluates long-horizon manipulation across three simulated embodiments and reports that leading agents still fail many subtasks, including frequent false claims of success.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors release a MuJoCo benchmark and report that the strongest tested configuration achieved 49.8% subtask success; they identify strategy choice, execution precision and incorrect success claims as recurring failure modes.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are from simulation, and the self-improvement findings include a five-task subset; physical-robot transfer and wider long-horizon generalization remain to be tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper was picked up by EmergentMind and Oscholar; its 22-task, five-seed-per-task simulation evaluation gives a concrete robotics signal, though external discussion was thinner than for the higher-ranked papers.
